To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fatigue life in bending of a 12 Cr martensitic steel is significantly improved by shot peening.

the fatigue crack growth behaviour of a 12 Cr martensitic steam blade material is affected both by the metallurgical defects (alumina stringers, manganese sulphide inclusions, carbides, etc.) and the shot peened defects (surface and subsurface) and that the most beneficial shot peened condition is the one which provides a known defect population and a compressively strained surface layer which can be used to substitute the underlying metallurgical defects.

“The fatigue crack growth behaviour in a shot-peened steam turbine blade alloy is dominated by the shot-peening induced compressive residual stresses, which are more important than the metallurgical defects (inclusions and stringers), which are present at the same time.”

the study of the three-dimensional morphology and development of fatigue cracks in a tempered martensitic alloy, which is used for steam turbine blades.
the three-dimensional morphology and behaviour of fatigue cracks, in particular in the presence of surface defects and the effects of surface treatments such as shot peening.
the development and validation of 3D imaging techniques and their application in fatigue crack growth studies in a 12% Cr tempered martensite steel.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fatigue crack initiation and growth behaviour in the shot peened condition is not controlled by the original metallurgical inclusions and stringers, but rather by the new defects introduced by the shot peening.
shot peening can be a useful surface engineering technique for improving the fatigue life of steam turbine blades, but only if the correct shot peening parameters are chosen.

the most beneficial shot peen condition is one that depletes the original metallurgical population of defects (e.g. by plastic deformation) and introduces a more benign population from the shot peen process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface conditions of the component can be used to control fatigue crack initiation and growth, and thus fatigue crack behaviour.
the shot peening defect population can be used to advantage to control fatigue crack initiation, propagation and arrest in a tempered martensitic steel.
shot peening can provide a different defect distribution that competes with the inherent metallurgical defects.
